I used all 100 simulations. The best design scores a **mean L/D of 115.8**, about 24% better than NACA 4412 (93.5). None of the 100 designs failed.

**Best design:** u = [0.44, 0.59, 0.60, 0.66, 0.45, 0.65, 0.645]
- **Thickness:** a0 ≈ 0.83, a2 ≈ 1.17, a3 ≈ 1.19. Maximum thickness sits at x/c ≈ 0.40.
- **Camber:** b ≈ [0.164, 0.080, 0.160, 0.158]. Maximum camber is 3.3% at x/c ≈ 0.56.

| CL | alpha | cd | L/D | cm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.4 | −0.42° | 0.00523 | 76.4 | −0.112 |
| 0.6 | 1.55° | 0.00493 | 121.7 | −0.107 |
| 0.8 | 2.94° | 0.00536 | 149.3 | −0.118 |

**What I learned about the design space**

1. **The amount of camber matters most.** The objective averages L/D, so CL = 0.8 counts the most, and the lowest drag should fall near CL 0.6–0.8. With uncambered or lightly cambered shapes (about 1.5%), drag climbs at CL 0.8. At 4.5–5.5% camber, CL 0.4 needs negative alpha, so drag rises on the lower surface. The best compromise was about 3.3–3.5% camber, which put minimum drag at CL ≈ 0.6.
2. **Moving thickness aft helps, but only to x/c ≈ 0.40.** Raising a2 lengthened the low-drag laminar flow. Beyond about x/c 0.45, especially with a sharp leading edge (u0 ≤ 0.3), CL 0.8 fell off a cliff: drag jumped to 0.013–0.017 and alpha to 5.5–6°. The likely cause is a pressure spike at the leading edge that moves transition far forward on the upper surface. Leading-edge bluntness and aft thickness have to be balanced: a0 ≈ 0.8–1.0 with a2 ≈ 1.1–1.3.
3. **The trailing-edge wedge (a3) has a narrow optimum.** Values near 1.0–1.2 were best. Very large values pushed max thickness to x/c 0.52 and drag up about 40% everywhere; very small values cost about 10%.
4. **Camber shape is a fine adjustment worth about 2–3 points.** The best shape is fairly uniform with a slight dip at b1 (mid-front). That trims about 3% off drag at CL 0.8 while keeping CL 0.4 acceptable. Pushing more camber towards the trailing edge raised the nose-down pitching moment (cm down to −0.135) and hurt CL 0.4. Strong leading-edge camber was neutral to slightly negative.
5. **The optimum is broad and flat.** The last ~30 designs all landed between 114.5 and 115.8. Differences that small are probably within XFoil's numerical noise, so my best design is effectively the centre of that plateau rather than a sharp peak. The main remaining trade-off is that lowering drag at CL 0.4 almost always cost drag at CL 0.8.
